title: Real Unfair Advantages: only what can't be copied or bought is a moat
summary: Anything that can be copied will be copied, including features, copy and pricing. Jason Cohen argues the only real competitive advantages are those that can't be copied or bought: insider knowledge, an obsessive hard One Thing, personal authority, a dream team, the right celebrity endorsement, and existing customers. Build toward them on purpose.

principles.text: Assume anything copyable will be copied; passion, hard work and being lean are not an edge.
principles.quote: Anything that *can* be copied *will* be copied, including features, marketing copy, and pricing.

principles.text: The only durable advantage is something competitors can neither copy nor buy.
principles.quote: The only real competitive advantage is that which cannot be copied and cannot be bought.

principles.text: Deep industry knowledge and pain-point insight is a legal unfair advantage that is hard for rivals to assemble.
principles.quote: using intimate knowledge of an industry and the specific pain points within an industry is a perfectly legal unfair advantage for a startup.

principles.text: Pick One Thing that is hard and refuse to lose on it; a merely unique feature is easily duplicated.
principles.quote: To remain un-copyable, your One Thing needs to be not just central to your existence, but also difficult to achieve.

principles.text: Authority can't be purchased; it takes years of effort, which is exactly why it is an untouchable edge.
principles.quote: **Authority cannot be purchased.** You can't raise VC money and then "have authority" in a year.

principles.text: A dream team (varied skills, common vision, insider knowledge) cuts startup risk and is hard to duplicate.
principles.quote: Of course a Dream Team doesn't guarantee success but it **significantly reduces the risk** of the startup, and furthermore is difficult for the competition to duplicate.
